test: Ohio BMV Driver License Knowledge Test (Class D / temporary permit)
edition: Based on the Ohio Driver Manual – Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (Ohio Department of Public Safety online edition, sections dated January 26, 2024, as published in October 2026), plus the Ohio Revised Code where noted

exam.rules: Ohio's knowledge test is required for a Temporary Instruction Permit Identification Card (TIPIC) and may be taken from age 15 years 6 months, either online through BMV Online Services (with a supervising adult if under 19; two attempts per six months) or in person at a Driver Exam Station or select Deputy Registrar agencies (unlimited attempts, one per day). It has 40 multiple-choice questions on motor vehicle laws and traffic signs and you need 75% (30 correct) to pass; under the Ohio Administrative Code the rules and signs portions are each scored at 75%. A vision screening is also required. If you fail, wait at least 24 hours before retesting. After passing, buy the TIPIC at a Deputy Registrar within 60 days. Applicants under 18 need a parent or guardian to co-sign; drivers under 21 must also complete driver education and 50 logged practice hours before the road test.

questions.q: What is the youngest age at which you may take the Ohio knowledge test to begin the temporary permit process?
questions.explain: Ohio lets applicants take the vision screening and knowledge test once they reach 15 years and six months of age.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 1: How to Get Your Driver License — 'Vision Screening and Knowledge Testing'; ORC 4507.05

questions.q: How many questions are on the Ohio driver license knowledge test?
questions.explain: The Ohio knowledge test has 40 multiple-choice questions covering traffic laws and traffic signs.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 1: How to Get Your Driver License — 'Knowledge Testing'; bmv.ohio.gov First Issuance page

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Ohio knowledge test?
questions.explain: Applicants must answer 75 percent of the questions correctly (30 of 40).
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 1: How to Get Your Driver License — 'Knowledge Testing'; OAC 4501:1-1-08

questions.q: If you fail the knowledge test at a Driver Exam Station, how soon may you retake it?
options: After waiting at least one day (24 hours)
questions.explain: A failed applicant must wait one day before retesting; in-person testing is limited to one attempt per day.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 1: How to Get Your Driver License — 'Vision Screening and Knowledge Testing'

questions.q: How many times may you attempt the Ohio knowledge test online?
options: Two attempts in a six-month period
questions.explain: Online knowledge testing through BMV Online Services is limited to two attempts in six months; in-person testing has no limit.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 1: How to Get Your Driver License — 'Knowledge Testing is available in the following ways'

questions.q: After passing the knowledge test and vision screening, within how many days must you buy your temporary permit (TIPIC)?
questions.explain: The TIPIC must be purchased at a Deputy Registrar within 60 days, or the applicant must retake the vision screening and knowledge test.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 1: How to Get Your Driver License — 'Temporary Instruction Permit Identification Card (TIPIC)'

questions.q: A 15-year-old permit holder wants to practice driving. Who may sit in the front passenger seat?
options: Any passenger with a temporary permit
A parent, guardian, custodian, licensed driving instructor, or an adult 21+ acting in place of a parent
Any licensed driver age 18 or older
Nobody is required in daylight hours
questions.explain: Under age 16, the permit holder must have a parent, guardian, custodian, licensed driving instructor, or a person 21+ acting in loco parentis beside them.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 1: How to Get Your Driver License — 'TIPIC Restrictions'

questions.q: A 16-year-old with a temporary permit may practice driving with any licensed driver of what age, except between midnight and 6 a.m.?
questions.explain: Permit holders aged 16–17 may drive with any valid licensed driver 21 or older, except from midnight to 6 a.m., when a parent, guardian or custodian is required.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 1: How to Get Your Driver License — 'TIPIC Restrictions'

questions.q: Which is TRUE for every Ohio temporary permit (TIPIC) holder, regardless of age?
options: Only the driver must wear a seat belt
Back-seat passengers need not wear belts
Driving alone is allowed in daylight
Use of any mobile electronic device while driving is prohibited
questions.explain: All TIPIC holders must carry the permit, may not use mobile electronic devices, and everyone must be belted; the supervising adult must not be intoxicated.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 1: How to Get Your Driver License — 'TIPIC Restrictions'

questions.q: How long must a driver under 18 hold a temporary permit before getting a probationary license?
questions.explain: Drivers under age 18 must hold the TIPIC for at least six months before the driving test.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 1: How to Get Your Driver License — 'Driver Education Requirements (Under Age 21)'

questions.q: How many hours of supervised practice driving must a driver under 21 log before getting an Ohio license?
options: 50 hours, including at least 10 at night
questions.explain: Drivers under 21 must log 50 hours of driving with an eligible adult, at least 10 of them at night, on form BMV 5791.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 1: How to Get Your Driver License — 'Driver Education Requirements (Under Age 21)'

questions.q: Ohio driver education for new drivers under 21 includes how much instruction?
options: 4 hours online and 4 hours behind the wheel
24 hours of classroom/online instruction and 8 hours of driving with an instructor
8 hours of classroom and 24 hours of driving
questions.explain: A licensed driver training school course has 24 hours of classroom or online instruction plus 8 hours of driving time.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 1: How to Get Your Driver License — 'Driver Education Requirements (Under Age 21)'

questions.q: During the first 12 months with a probationary license, a driver under 18 may not drive during which hours unless an exception applies?
questions.explain: For the first 12 months, the curfew is midnight to 6 a.m. unless with a parent/guardian or driving to/from work, school or religious events with documentation.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 12: Purchase Your Driver License — 'Class D Operator's License — New drivers under age 18'

questions.q: After holding a probationary license for 12 months, a driver who is still under 18 may not drive during which hours (unless an exception applies)?
options: There are no hour limits after 12 months
questions.explain: After the first 12 months and until age 18, the restricted hours shrink to 1 a.m.–5 a.m.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 12: Purchase Your Driver License — 'Class D Operator's License — After the first 12 months'

questions.q: During the first 12 months of a probationary license, how many non-family passengers may a driver under 18 carry without a parent or guardian present?
questions.explain: Until the first 12 months are up, a driver under 18 may carry only one passenger from outside the family, unless a parent or guardian is riding along.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 12: Purchase Your Driver License — 'Class D Operator's License — New drivers under age 18'

questions.q: A 16-year-old probationary driver is convicted of a traffic offense within the first six months of licensure. What may result?
options: Only a written warning is sent
The driver must retake only the vision test
A parent or guardian may have to accompany the driver for six months or until age 17
questions.explain: A conviction in the first six months can require a parent or guardian to ride along for six months or until the driver turns 17.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 12: Purchase Your Driver License — 'Class D Operator's License'

questions.q: Who must co-sign the license or permit application of an applicant under 18?
questions.explain: A parent or guardian must be present to co-sign for an applicant under 18, and is jointly liable for the minor's negligent driving until age 18.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 12: Purchase Your Driver License — 'Co-signer Responsibility'; ORC 4507.07

questions.q: When does an Ohio driver license issued to someone under 21 expire?
options: Four years after issue regardless of age
questions.explain: A license issued to a driver under 21 expires on the 21st birthday and must be renewed in person.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 12: Purchase Your Driver License — 'Renewing Your Driver License'

questions.q: New residents of Ohio must obtain an Ohio driver license within how many days of establishing residency?
questions.explain: Ohio requires new residents to get an Ohio-issued driver license within 30 days of establishing residency.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 13: What Else Should I Know? — 'New Ohio Residents'

questions.q: An applicant age 21 or older fails the Ohio driving (road/maneuverability) test on the first try. What is generally required before the second attempt?
options: Complete an abbreviated adult driver training course
questions.explain: Applicants 21+ who fail the first driving test must complete the Abbreviated Adult Driver Training Course unless they took approved driver education within the past year.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 11: Taking the Driving Test — 'Abbreviated Adult Driver Training Course'; OAC 4501-8

questions.q: What is the minimum tire tread depth Ohio considers safe?
questions.explain: A tire in safe condition has at least 1/16-inch of tread and no major bumps, bulges or damage.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 2: Before You Drive — 'Tire Safety'

questions.q: During which period are studded tires legal in Ohio?
questions.explain: Studded tires may be used in Ohio from November 1 through April 15.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 2: Before You Drive — 'Tire Safety'

questions.q: In Ohio, what are the minimum liability insurance limits?
options: $25,000 per person, $50,000 per crash for injury/death, $25,000 property damage
questions.explain: Ohio's minimum financial responsibility is 25/50/25.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 6: State Laws and Penalties — 'Insurance - Financial Responsibility'; ORC 4509.101

questions.q: What does this sign require you to do?
options: Stop only if other vehicles are present
Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe
Slow down and go without stopping if clear
questions.explain: This red octagon requires all traffic in the lane to stop completely before proceeding.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Traffic Signs — Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What should you do when you reach this sign?
options: Speed up to merge ahead of traffic
Slow down, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and stop if necessary
Proceed without slowing; others must yield to you
Always come to a full stop
questions.explain: The triangular sign means you stop only if other traffic is affected and must yield to oncoming/crossing traffic.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Traffic Signs — Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: One-way traffic coming toward you; enter with caution
You may not enter this road from your direction
questions.explain: This sign is used at one-way roads and freeway exit ramps to stop drivers entering against traffic.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Traffic Signs — Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: You see this sign facing you. What does it tell you?
options: You are on the wrong exit; continue to the next one
You are traveling against traffic and must safely turn around or exit
questions.explain: This sign warns that you have entered a one-way roadway or ramp in the wrong direction.
questions.ref: MUTCD regulatory sign (R5-1a), as used on Ohio roads; Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Traffic Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The maximum lawful speed under good conditions is 55 mph
The recommended speed in curves is 55 mph
You must always drive exactly 55 mph
questions.explain: Posted limits are the maximum reasonable speed in good conditions; Ohio's assured-clear-distance rule may require going slower.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Speed Limits'; ORC 4511.21

questions.q: What does this sign prohibit?
questions.explain: A red circle with a slash means 'no'; the arrow shows the prohibited move—here, a left turn.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Traffic Signs — Prohibitory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
questions.explain: The red circle and slash over a U-shaped arrow prohibits U-turns.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Traffic Signs — Prohibitory Signs'

questions.q: At an intersection with this sign and a red light, what must you do?
options: Turn right after a full stop
Turn left after a full stop
Turn right without stopping if clear
Wait for a green signal before turning
questions.explain: Ohio normally allows a right turn on red after a full stop, but not where a sign prohibits it.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Turning on a Red Traffic Signal'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: Traffic on this road moves only in the direction of the arrow
Detour in the direction of the arrow
The road ahead curves in that direction
You must turn in the direction of the arrow
questions.explain: This sign indicates a one-way road.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Traffic Signs — Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Passing other vehicles is not allowed here
questions.explain: This regulatory sign marks a section where passing is prohibited, usually backed by a solid yellow line on your side.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Passing'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you when your light is a solid green ball?
options: Oncoming traffic must stop for you
Left turns are prohibited on green
You have the right-of-way to turn left
You may turn left but must yield to oncoming traffic
questions.explain: A green ball is not a protected turn; when turning left, yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Left Turns'

questions.q: What should you do when you see this sign at a crossing?
options: Speed up to clear the tracks quickly
Slow down, look and listen, and be prepared to stop for a train
Stop every time, even if no train is near
questions.explain: The white crossbuck marks a railroad grade crossing; slow down and be ready to stop if you see or hear a train.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Railroad Crossings'

questions.q: What does this round yellow sign warn you about?
questions.explain: The round yellow sign with an X and 'RR' gives advance warning of a highway-railroad crossing.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Railroad Crossings'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: A sharp right turn at an intersection
Side road enters from the right
The road curves to the right ahead
questions.explain: This warning sign shows a curve ahead; reduce speed before entering the curve.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Curves'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
questions.explain: The right-angle arrow warns of a sharp right turn; slow down significantly.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The road you are on ends ahead; you must turn left or right
A side road joins from both sides; continue straight
questions.explain: The T-shaped symbol warns of an intersection where you must turn left or right.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Warning Signs — Intersection ahead; Turn left or right'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
options: A side road on the right is closed
Your lane ends and you must merge right
Traffic will be merging into your road from the right
questions.explain: This warning sign alerts you to traffic merging from the right; adjust speed or position to let it merge.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Space to the Side'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The right lane ends ahead; traffic must merge left
A new lane is added on the right
questions.explain: This warning sign shows the right lane ending; drivers in that lane must merge left when safe.
questions.ref: MUTCD warning sign (W4-2); Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Changing Lanes'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: Two-way traffic ahead; oncoming traffic will share the road
questions.explain: This sign warns that traffic travels in opposite directions ahead.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Warning Signs — Traffic travels in opposite directions'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
options: A stop sign at the next corner only
questions.explain: This warning sign tells you there is a traffic signal ahead; be prepared to stop.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: The road can be slippery when it is wet
questions.explain: Reduce speed and avoid sudden braking or turning; wet roads reduce tire grip.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Slippery Roads'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
options: Trucks must use the left lane
questions.explain: This sign warns of a downhill grade; check your speed and be ready to use a lower gear.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Warning Signs — Downhill grade ahead'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
questions.explain: This warning sign alerts you that pedestrians may be crossing; be ready to yield.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Warning Signs — Pedestrian crossing ahead'

questions.q: What does this five-sided sign warn you about?
options: A school zone or school crossing ahead
A playground with no speed rules
questions.explain: The pentagon shape is used for school zones and crossings; in Ohio, school zones commonly have a 20 mph limit during restricted hours.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Speed Limits; Regulatory Signs'; ORC 4511.21(B)(1)

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
questions.explain: This warning sign means bicyclists may be crossing or entering the roadway.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Warning Signs — Bicycle crossing'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
options: A lane width of 12 feet 6 inches
questions.explain: This sign gives the height of a low overpass or structure; taller vehicles must not pass under it.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Warning Signs — Limited clearance ahead'

questions.q: Where is this pennant-shaped sign placed, and what does it mean?
options: Over the road; it marks a toll
On the left side of the road; it marks the start of a no-passing zone
On the left; it means passing is allowed with care
On the right side; it marks the end of a no-passing zone
questions.explain: The yellow pennant on the left side of the road marks the beginning of a no-passing zone.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Warning Signs — Passing is prohibited'

questions.q: This yellow plaque is posted under a curve sign. What does it mean?
options: The speed limit for trucks only
The legal limit for the next 35 miles
The recommended safe speed through the curve is 35 mph
questions.explain: An advisory speed plaque shows the safe speed for the hazard under normal conditions.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Curves'

questions.q: What should you do when you see this orange sign?
options: Use the shoulder to pass slow traffic
Ignore it if no workers are visible
Be alert, slow down, and watch for workers and equipment
Speed up to clear the area quickly
questions.explain: Orange signs mark work zones; reduce speed even if no workers are present—speeding fines can be doubled.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 7: Special Driving Situations — 'Work Zones'

questions.q: A vehicle displays this emblem on its rear. What does it tell you?
options: The vehicle is towing a wide load
The vehicle travels at less than 25 mph
The vehicle is an emergency vehicle
questions.explain: The orange-and-red triangle marks slow-moving vehicles (farm, construction, animal-drawn) traveling under 25 mph.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Slow Moving Vehicles'; ORC 4511.31

questions.q: What does this sign indicate?
options: Free parking for anyone for 15 minutes
Parking reserved for people with a disability placard or plate
questions.explain: You may not park in a space marked with the wheelchair symbol without an issued placard or accessible plate.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'No-Parking Zones / Handicapped Spaces'

questions.q: What must you do at this signal?
options: Stop completely, then proceed when the way is clear
Stop only if cross traffic is present
Wait for the light to turn green
Slow down and proceed without stopping
questions.explain: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Traffic Signals — Flashing Red'; ORC 4511.13

questions.q: What does this signal mean?
options: The signal is broken; treat it as a four-way stop
Slow down and proceed with caution
questions.explain: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed with caution, and be ready to stop for entering traffic.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Traffic Signals — Flashing Yellow'

questions.q: What does a steady signal like this mean?
options: The light is about to turn red; prepare to stop
Speed up to beat the red light
Stop only if a pedestrian is crossing
The same as a flashing yellow light
questions.explain: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to change to red.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Traffic Signals — Yellow'

questions.q: What does this signal allow?
options: Turning left only after yielding to oncoming traffic that has a green light
Turning left in the direction of the arrow without stopping
questions.explain: A green arrow means you may turn in the direction of the arrow; oncoming traffic is held. Still yield to anyone already in the intersection.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Traffic Signals — Green'

questions.q: Unless a sign prohibits it, what may you do at this signal?
options: Turn right after a complete stop, yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic
Turn left onto a two-way street after stopping
Go straight after stopping if clear
questions.explain: Ohio allows a right turn on red after a full stop, yielding to all crossing traffic and pedestrians, unless posted otherwise.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Turning on a Red Traffic Signal'

questions.q: What do these center lines mean?
options: Passing is allowed only for the lane on the right
Passing is allowed with care in both directions
Passing is not allowed in either direction
The lanes are for left turns only
questions.explain: A double solid yellow line prohibits passing; you may cross it only to turn left or to pass a slow-moving vehicle where allowed.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Lane Pavement Markings — Yellow Solid Double Line'

questions.q: What does this center line mean on a two-lane road?
options: Traffic travels in one direction only
Drivers in either direction may pass when it is safe
This is a two-way left-turn lane
questions.explain: A broken yellow center line lets vehicles in either direction pass when safe.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Lane Pavement Markings — Yellow Broken Line'

questions.q: What is the center lane marked like this used for?
options: Left turns by traffic from either direction
questions.explain: A two-way left-turn lane is only for vehicles about to turn left—not for traveling or passing.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Two-way Left Turn Only Lane'

questions.q: Warning signs on Ohio roads are usually what shape and color?
options: Yellow diamonds with black symbols or letters
questions.explain: Warning signs are generally yellow with black lettering or symbols and diamond shaped.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: Signs with an orange background are used for:
questions.explain: Work zone signs have a distinctive orange background with black letters or symbols.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Work Zone Signs'

questions.q: A red circle with a diagonal slash on a sign means:
options: The action is allowed only at night
questions.explain: The red circle with a slash represents the word 'NO'.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Prohibitory Signs'

questions.q: Blue guide signs along the highway usually tell you about:
options: Motorist services such as gas, food, lodging or hospitals
questions.explain: Guide signs may be green, brown or blue; blue signs show services like gas stations, hotels and hospitals.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Guide Signs'

questions.q: A traffic signal at an intersection is dark because of a power outage and no officer is directing traffic. What must you do?
options: Proceed without stopping if you are on the larger road
Yield only to traffic on your right without stopping
Treat the intersection as a four-way stop
questions.explain: By law, a non-working signal is treated as a four-way (all-way) stop unless an officer is directing traffic.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 10: Emergency Situations — 'Inoperable Traffic Signals'

questions.q: On a two-lane road the center has a solid yellow line on your side and a broken yellow line on the other side. What does this mean for you?
options: Only oncoming traffic must not pass
questions.explain: Passing is prohibited for drivers on the side with the solid line; drivers on the broken-line side may pass when safe.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Lane Pavement Markings — Yellow Solid Line with a Broken Line'

questions.q: Two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time. Who should go first?
questions.explain: When both arrive at the same time, yield to the driver on your right.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Right-of-Way'

questions.q: At an intersection, who should generally get the right-of-way?
options: The driver on the wider road always
The driver who arrived at the intersection first
questions.explain: Yield to a driver who is already at, or who arrives before you at, the intersection.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Right-of-Way'

questions.q: You are turning left at an intersection with a green light (no arrow). Whom must you yield to?
options: Oncoming traffic and pedestrians in the crosswalk
No one; green gives you the right-of-way
questions.explain: When turning left, yield to drivers in the opposing lanes and to pedestrians.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Left Turns'

questions.q: You are pulling out of a private driveway onto a public road. Who has the right-of-way?
options: Traffic already on the public road
questions.explain: Drivers entering from a driveway or private road must yield to drivers on the public highway.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Right-of-Way'

questions.q: When emerging from an alley or driveway in a business or residential district, you must:
options: Sound your horn and drive across the sidewalk
Slow down but stopping is not required
Stop before the sidewalk (or before the roadway if there is no sidewalk) and yield to pedestrians
Stop only if a car is coming
questions.explain: Ohio law requires a stop at the sidewalk area, or before entering the roadway if none, and yielding to pedestrians.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping the Vehicle — A driver must stop'

questions.q: On a freeway entrance ramp, who has the right-of-way?
options: Vehicles already traveling on the freeway
Vehicles in the left lane only
questions.explain: Drivers on an entrance or acceleration ramp must yield to drivers already on the limited-access highway.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Right-of-Way'

questions.q: A police car, fire truck or ambulance with flashing lights and siren approaches from behind. What should you do?
options: Pull to the right edge of the road, stop, and stay there until it passes
Speed up to clear the way
questions.explain: Move as far right as possible and remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, without blocking intersections.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Emergency Vehicles'; ORC 4511.45

questions.q: An emergency vehicle with lights and siren is approaching from the opposite direction on a divided highway. What does Ohio law say?
options: You must pull right and stop
You must stop in your lane
You must pull to the left shoulder
You are not required to stop for it
questions.explain: The duty to pull over and stop does not apply to an emergency vehicle traveling in the opposite direction on a divided highway.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping the Vehicle — A driver must stop'

questions.q: A funeral procession is passing through an intersection where your light is green. What should you do?
options: Honk so they let you through
Proceed because you have a green light
Cut into the procession when there is a gap
questions.explain: Ohio drivers are told to yield the right-of-way to funeral processions.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Right-of-Way'

questions.q: Your light turns green, but a pedestrian is still crossing in front of you. What should you do?
options: Wait until the pedestrian has cleared your path
Proceed; the pedestrian must yield to green
questions.explain: You must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and drivers still in the intersection.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Right-of-Way'

questions.q: A pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog is about to cross. What should you do?
options: Yield; the pedestrian has the right-of-way
Flash your headlights to signal them to cross
questions.explain: Pedestrians who are blind or visually impaired (white cane or guide dog) have the right-of-way.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Pedestrians'

questions.q: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to:
options: Traffic on your right that is entering
No one; entering traffic has priority
Traffic already circulating in the roundabout
Traffic waiting to enter behind you
questions.explain: Entering traffic yields to circulating traffic; look left and enter when the lane is clear.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Roundabouts and Traffic Circles'

questions.q: In which direction do vehicles travel around a roundabout in Ohio?
options: Whichever way the first car goes
questions.explain: Vehicles travel counterclockwise around the center island.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Roundabouts and Traffic Circles'

questions.q: Once you are inside a roundabout, you should:
options: Stop at each exit to check traffic
Stop to let entering traffic in
Change lanes as needed to pass
Keep moving and not change lanes until you exit
questions.explain: Once in the roundabout, keep moving; do not stop or change lanes.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Roundabouts and Traffic Circles'

questions.q: In a typical four-exit roundabout, which exit do you use to make a left turn?
questions.explain: First exit = right, second = straight, third = left, fourth = U-turn.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Roundabouts and Traffic Circles'

questions.q: Your light is green, but traffic is backed up on the other side of the intersection. What should you do?
options: Wait before the intersection until there is room for your vehicle on the other side
questions.explain: You must stop before entering an intersection if there is not enough space on the other side, even with a green light.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping the Vehicle; Tips'

questions.q: You are at a stop sign and cannot see cross traffic because of parked cars. What should you do?
options: After stopping, edge forward slowly until you can see, then proceed when clear
Back up and find another route
Proceed quickly to cut your exposure time
questions.explain: Stop first, then creep forward to check for traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Tips'

questions.q: A stop is required but there is no stop line or crosswalk. Where should you stop?
options: In the middle of the intersection
At the point nearest the intersecting road where you can see approaching traffic, before entering it
You need not stop if there is no line
Anywhere within 100 feet of the corner
questions.explain: Without a line or crosswalk, stop where you can see traffic on the intersecting roadway before actually entering it.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping the Vehicle'; ORC 4511.43; BMV Sample Knowledge Test topic

questions.q: On a one-lane bridge or roadway with a sign saying the nearest vehicle has the right-of-way, who goes first?
options: The vehicle that flashes its headlights
The vehicle that is nearest the bridge
questions.explain: Ohio's warning sign for a one-lane bridge indicates that the vehicle nearest the bridge has the right-of-way.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Warning Signs — Vehicle nearest the bridge has the right-of-way'

questions.q: You approach a stopped police car with its lights flashing on the shoulder of a multi-lane highway. What does Ohio's move-over law require?
options: Use the shoulder on the other side
Maintain speed and stay in your lane
Move to a lane not next to it if safe; if not, slow down and proceed with caution
questions.explain: Ohio requires moving over a lane when safe, or slowing down and proceeding with caution if a lane change is not safe.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Move Over Laws'; ORC 4511.213

questions.q: Ohio's move-over law applies to which of these when stopped with warning lights on?
options: A parked delivery van with hazard lights
A school bus loading children (different rule)
Any car with a flat tire
questions.explain: The law covers emergency vehicles, road service vehicles (tow trucks, snowplows), waste collection, highway maintenance and PUCO vehicles with lights activated.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Move Over Laws'; ORC 4511.213

questions.q: You are driving on a two-lane road and meet a school bus stopped with red lights flashing. What must you do?
options: Stop only if children are visible
Slow to 20 mph and pass carefully
Stop only if you are behind the bus
Stop at least 10 feet from the bus, whichever direction you are traveling
questions.explain: On roads with fewer than four lanes, traffic from both directions must stop at least 10 feet from the bus until it moves or the driver signals.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping for a School Bus'; ORC 4511.75

questions.q: A school bus is stopped with red lights flashing on a highway with four or more lanes. Which vehicles must stop?
options: Only vehicles traveling in the same direction as the bus
Only vehicles in the lane next to the bus
No vehicles, because the road is wide
questions.explain: On a road with four or more traffic lanes, only traffic moving in the same direction as the bus must stop.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping for a School Bus'; ORC 4511.75(C)

questions.q: A school bus begins flashing its amber (yellow) lights. What do they mean?
options: You may pass the bus quickly
The bus is preparing to stop; get ready to stop
questions.explain: Amber lights warn that the bus is about to stop; you are not required to stop yet but should prepare to.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping for a School Bus'

questions.q: A stopped school bus with flashing red lights has no stop arm extended. Must you stop?
options: No, only the stop arm requires a stop
questions.explain: Even if the bus has no stop arm, you are still required to stop.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping for a School Bus'; ORC 4511.75(A)

questions.q: After stopping for a school bus with red lights flashing, when may you proceed?
options: When no children are on the road
When the bus starts moving or the bus driver signals you to go
When the stop arm starts to fold
questions.explain: Remain stopped until the bus resumes motion or the driver signals motorists to proceed.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping for a School Bus'; ORC 4511.75

questions.q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on streets within an Ohio municipality (city or village)?
questions.explain: The prima-facie limit for streets within a municipal corporation is 25 mph.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Speed Limits'; ORC 4511.21(B)(2)

questions.q: What is the speed limit in an Ohio school zone during recess and while children are going to or leaving school?
questions.explain: School zones have a 20 mph limit during the restricted times when posted.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Speed Limits'; ORC 4511.21(B)(1)(a)

questions.q: What is the speed limit in an alley within an Ohio municipality?
questions.explain: Alleys within a municipal corporation have a 15 mph limit.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Speed Limits'; ORC 4511.21(B)(7)

questions.q: What is the maximum speed limit on Ohio's rural freeways (such as rural interstates)?
questions.explain: Rural freeways have a 70 mph limit.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Speed Limits'; ORC 4511.21(B)(14)

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on freeways with paved shoulders inside an Ohio municipality?
questions.explain: Freeways with paved shoulders inside municipal corporations are limited to 55 mph unless posted otherwise.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Speed Limits'; ORC 4511.21(B)(11)

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on state routes or through highways within a municipality, outside business districts?
questions.explain: State routes or through highways within municipalities outside business districts have a 35 mph limit.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Speed Limits'; ORC 4511.21(B)(3)

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on state routes within a municipality but outside urban districts?
questions.explain: State routes inside municipal corporations but outside urban districts are 50 mph unless a lower limit is set.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Speed Limits'; ORC 4511.21(B)(6)

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, what is the general speed limit on highways outside municipalities (not freeways or expressways)?
questions.explain: Ohio's general limit on highways outside municipal corporations is 55 mph.
questions.ref: ORC 4511.21(B)(5); Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: Ohio's 'assured clear distance ahead' rule means you must:
options: Always drive at the posted limit
Keep at least 100 feet behind any vehicle
Drive no faster than lets you stop within the distance you can see ahead
questions.explain: Regardless of the posted limit, Ohio law prohibits a speed greater than will let you stop in the distance available.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Speed Limits'; ORC 4511.21(A)

questions.q: Posted speed limits are set for which conditions?
options: Dry weather, good visibility and expected traffic
questions.explain: Limits assume dry weather without fog; in poor conditions a reasonable speed may be lower than the limit.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: What minimum following distance does the Ohio Driver Manual recommend behind the vehicle ahead?
questions.explain: Keep at least four seconds (or one vehicle length per 10 mph) between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Space to the Front'

questions.q: Besides the four-second rule, the Ohio manual suggests a following distance of at least:
options: One vehicle length for every 10 mph of speed
Two vehicle lengths at any speed
One vehicle length for every 20 mph
questions.explain: The manual's rule of thumb is one vehicle length per 10 mph, or four seconds.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Space to the Front'

questions.q: How do you check a four-second following distance?
options: Watch your speedometer for four seconds
Count seconds from when the vehicle ahead passes a fixed object until you reach it
Count the dashes on the road between you
Count the cars ahead of you
questions.explain: When the rear of the vehicle ahead passes a fixed point, count; if you reach it before four seconds, you are too close.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Space to the Front'

questions.q: In which situation should you increase your following distance beyond four seconds?
options: When driving below the speed limit
Driving on a dry road in daylight
Following a vehicle that must stop at railroad crossings, such as a bus
When the car behind you is far back
questions.explain: Increase distance in bad weather or at night, on slippery roads, behind large vehicles, and behind vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Space to the Front'

questions.q: How far ahead should you try to look while driving?
options: Only to the car directly ahead
questions.explain: The manual recommends looking 20–30 seconds ahead to plan your movements.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Look Ahead'

questions.q: According to the Ohio manual, about how far does it take to brake to a stop from 50 mph on dry pavement with good brakes (braking distance only)?
questions.explain: At 50 mph on dry pavement, braking alone can take about 158 feet—before adding perception and reaction distance.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Stopping Distance = Space Cushion'

questions.q: What is the average perception time for an alert driver?
questions.explain: Both average perception time and reaction time are about 3/4 to 1 second.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Stopping Distance = Space Cushion'

questions.q: You should reduce your speed before entering a curve so that you can:
options: Use slight, steady acceleration through the curve
Shift to neutral through the curve
Brake hard in the middle of the curve
questions.explain: Slow before the curve, then apply slight and constant acceleration through it.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Curves'

questions.q: Speeding in an Ohio work zone can result in:
options: Doubled fines and possible jail time
A fine only if workers are hurt
questions.explain: Ohio treats work-zone speeding seriously: the fine can be doubled and jail time is possible.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 4: Rules of the Road — 'Work Zone Signs'

questions.q: Which places ice first in winter?
questions.explain: Bridges, overpasses and shaded areas freeze before the rest of the road.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 7: Special Driving Situations — 'Winter Driving'

questions.q: What is the most important thing to do to avoid crashes on snowy or icy roads?
options: Engage four-wheel drive and keep normal speed
Reduce speed and increase following distance
Drive close to the car ahead to follow its tracks
questions.explain: Slower speeds and greater following distance are needed because stopping distances grow on slippery roads.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 7: Special Driving Situations — 'Winter Driving'; BMV Sample Knowledge Test topic

questions.q: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?
options: Speed up to get through water quickly
Slow down when the road is wet or has standing water
Brake hard when you see puddles
Inflate tires above the recommended pressure
questions.explain: Hydroplaning is avoided mainly by slowing down on wet roads with pooled water.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Hydroplaning'

questions.q: How far before a turn must you signal in Ohio?
questions.explain: A turn signal must be given continuously for at least the last 100 feet before turning.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Turn Signal'; ORC 4511.39

questions.q: What does a driver's left arm extended straight out the window mean?
questions.explain: Arm straight out is the hand signal for a left turn.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Turn Signal'

questions.q: What does a driver's left arm bent upward at a 90-degree angle mean?
questions.explain: Arm bent upward signals a right turn.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Turn Signal'

questions.q: What does a driver's left arm extended downward mean?
questions.explain: Arm pointing downward signals slow or stop.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Turn Signal'

questions.q: When making a right turn, you should:
options: Turn into the far left lane
Turn from the right-most part of your lane into the right-most part of the new street
Swing wide to the left first
questions.explain: Avoid swinging wide; turn from the right portion of your lane into the right portion of the new road.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Right Turns'

questions.q: When making a left turn onto a two-way street, you should turn into:
options: The lane just to the right of the center line
questions.explain: Turn from the left-most part of your lane into the left-most lane just right of the center line.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Left Turns'

questions.q: While waiting to turn left at a green light with heavy oncoming traffic, you should:
options: Position the front of the car slightly past the stop bar and turn when it is safe
Turn your wheels left while waiting
Go around the left side of the oncoming traffic
Wait behind the stop line until the light turns red, then go straight
questions.explain: If oncoming traffic leaves no gap, pull just past the stop bar, keep yielding to oncoming cars and pedestrians, and complete the turn once it is safe.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Left Turns'

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light permitted in Ohio?
options: Only when a police officer is absent
From the far-left lane of a one-way street onto another one-way street, after stopping, unless prohibited
From any street after a full stop
questions.explain: Ohio permits a left on red only when you are in the leftmost lane of a one-way street turning onto another one-way street, after a full stop and only if no sign prohibits it.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Left Turn on Red'

questions.q: Before turning right on a red light, you must:
options: Come to a complete stop and let all crossing traffic and pedestrians clear
questions.explain: A right turn on red requires a full stop and yielding to all crossing traffic and pedestrians.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Right Turn on Red'

questions.q: At an intersection with two left-turn lanes, you should:
options: Use either lane but end in the right lane
Pick a lane and stay in it until the turn is complete
Switch lanes during the turn if the other is clear
questions.explain: For multiple-lane turns, enter the lane you will turn from and stay in that lane through the turn.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Multiple Lane Turning'

questions.q: On a road with four or more lanes, which lane should you normally drive in?
options: The right lane, using the lane just right of center to pass or turn left
questions.explain: On roads with four or more lanes, normal driving belongs in the right lane; the lane next to the center is for passing and left turns.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Lane Travel'

questions.q: When changing lanes, how do you check your blind spot?
options: Rely on the side mirror only
Turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move
questions.explain: Mirrors leave blind spots; turn your head and look before moving over.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Changing Lanes'

questions.q: When passing another vehicle, return to your lane when:
options: The other driver flashes their lights
You have traveled 100 feet past it
Your rear bumper clears its front bumper
You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rear-view mirror
questions.explain: Continue until both headlights of the vehicle you passed are visible in the inside mirror.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Passing'

questions.q: Where is passing NOT permitted?
options: On a multi-lane highway in the left lane
On a straight road with a broken yellow line
Within an intersection or approaching a railroad crossing
On a one-way street with two lanes, when safe
questions.explain: Do not pass at intersections, before a railroad crossing or bridge, on curves or hills, or with oncoming traffic approaching.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Passing'

questions.q: Is passing on the shoulder of the road allowed?
options: No, never—whether the shoulder is paved or not
Yes, to pass a left-turning vehicle
questions.explain: The Ohio manual says never pass on the shoulder, paved or unpaved.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Multi-Lane, Two-Way Roadway'

questions.q: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:
options: Stay in your lane and keep a steady speed
questions.explain: Stay in your lane and maintain a constant speed so the other driver can pass.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Passing'

questions.q: When may you cross a double solid yellow center line?
options: To pass any vehicle going under the limit
To turn left into a driveway, or to pass a slow-moving vehicle when safe
questions.explain: Crossing is permitted only to turn left into a driveway or to pass a slow-moving vehicle (e.g., bicycle or SMV) when safe.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Solid Double Yellow Lines'

questions.q: You may cross a solid yellow line to pass a slow-moving vehicle only if it is going less than what speed?
questions.explain: You may pass a slow-moving vehicle across a solid yellow line if it travels less than half the posted limit, you do not exceed the limit, and there is enough clear space.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Slow Moving Vehicles'; ORC 4511.31

questions.q: A two-way center left-turn lane may be used for:
options: Left turns only, immediately before turning
Merging into traffic from the right
questions.explain: This lane is reserved for left-turning vehicles and is not used for passing, merging or traveling.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Center Two-Way Left Turn Lane'

questions.q: When entering a freeway, you should:
options: Enter without signaling if traffic is light
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait
Signal and use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, then merge into a gap
questions.explain: Use the acceleration lane to match traffic speed, find a gap, signal and merge, then cancel the signal.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Entering a Multi-lane Highway'

questions.q: You missed your freeway exit. What should you do?
options: Stop and wait for a gap to cut across
Use a median crossover to turn around
questions.explain: Take the next exit; median openings are only for emergency and public safety vehicles.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Exiting a Roadway'

questions.q: When exiting a freeway, where should you begin to slow down?
options: On the main roadway before the exit
questions.explain: Maintain speed on the main road, signal, move into the deceleration lane, then slow down.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Exiting a Roadway'

questions.q: Ohio law requires you to drive on the right half of the road EXCEPT when:
options: You are about to turn right
Passing a vehicle going the same direction when it is safe
questions.explain: Exceptions include passing, roads with three or more marked lanes, one-way roads, obstructions, or direction by an officer.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Lane Travel'; ORC 4511.25

questions.q: When backing up, where should you place your hands and look?
options: Left hand at 12 o'clock on the wheel, turn and look through the rear window
Both hands at 9 and 3 while watching the backup camera only
Look forward and use the horn
questions.explain: Grasp the wheel at 12 o'clock with your left hand, put your right arm on the passenger seat, and look directly back.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Backing Up'

questions.q: Where does the Ohio Driver Manual recommend placing your hands on the steering wheel?
options: At about the 4 and 8 o'clock positions
questions.explain: The manual recommends hands at 4 and 8 o'clock for control and to stay clear of a deploying air bag.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Steering'

questions.q: How close to a fire hydrant may you park in Ohio?
questions.explain: Ohio prohibits stopping, standing or parking within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping, Parking, or Standing Prohibited'; ORC 4511.68(A)(4)

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk at an intersection?
questions.explain: Parking is prohibited within 20 feet of an intersection or crosswalk.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping, Parking, or Standing Prohibited'; ORC 4511.68(A)(6)

questions.q: When parallel parking, your vehicle must be no more than how far from the curb?
questions.explain: Park parallel to and not more than 12 inches from the curb, facing the direction of traffic.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Parking'

questions.q: On a two-way street, which way must your parked vehicle face?
options: In the direction of traffic on that side of the street
questions.explain: Vehicles must be parked facing the direction of traffic, parallel to the right curb.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Parking'

questions.q: On a one-way street, where may you parallel park?
options: Within 12 inches of either the right or left curb
questions.explain: On one-way streets, you may park within 12 inches of the right or left curb.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Parking'

questions.q: How close may you park to the nearest rail of a railroad crossing?
questions.explain: Ohio law prohibits parking within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.
questions.ref: ORC 4511.68(A)(9); Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping, Parking, or Standing Prohibited'

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of the approach to a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal?
questions.explain: Ohio law prohibits standing or parking within 30 feet of, and on the approach to, a stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal.
questions.ref: ORC 4511.68(A)(7); Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping, Parking, or Standing Prohibited'

questions.q: Which of these is a place where you may NOT stop, stand or park?
options: In a driveway on your own property
In a marked parking space along the curb
Alongside a vehicle already parked at the curb (double parking)
questions.explain: Ohio prohibits stopping or parking alongside a vehicle stopped or parked at the curb.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping, Parking, or Standing Prohibited'; ORC 4511.68

questions.q: Which of these vehicles may be parked on a sidewalk in Ohio if it does not block pedestrians?
options: A motorcycle with a 600 cc engine
questions.explain: Bicycles, e-bikes, mopeds, scooters of 150 cc or less and micro-mobility devices may park on a sidewalk if pedestrian flow is not impeded.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping, Parking, or Standing Prohibited'; ORC 4511.68(B)

questions.q: When parking on a hill next to a curb, the Ohio manual says you should turn your front wheels:
options: Away from any curb in all cases
Toward the curb side of the road, then shift to park and set the parking brake
It does not matter if the parking brake is set
questions.explain: Turn the front wheels toward the curb side, shift to PARK, set the parking brake and turn off the engine.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Parking on a Hill or Grade'

questions.q: May you park in front of a public or private driveway?
options: Yes, if you stay in the car
questions.explain: Stopping, standing or parking in front of a public or private driveway is prohibited.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping, Parking, or Standing Prohibited'; ORC 4511.68(A)(2)

questions.q: How close may you park to another parked vehicle?
questions.explain: Ohio prohibits parking within one foot of another parked vehicle.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Stopping, Parking, or Standing Prohibited'; ORC 4511.68(A)(15)

questions.q: Who may park in a space marked with the wheelchair symbol?
options: Only a vehicle displaying an issued disability placard or accessible license plate
questions.explain: Spaces with the wheelchair symbol are reserved; you need an issued disability placard or accessible plate to use one.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'No-Parking Zones / Handicapped Spaces'

questions.q: Is it legal to park on a bridge or in a highway tunnel in Ohio?
options: No, unless directed by an officer or traffic control device
Yes, if hazard lights are on
questions.explain: ORC 4511.68 lists bridges, elevated structures and highway tunnels as no-stopping/parking places.

questions.q: When passing a bicyclist, Ohio law requires you to leave at least how much space?
questions.explain: Maintain a safety zone of at least three feet between your vehicle and a bicycle.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Bicyclists'; ORC 4511.27

questions.q: On Ohio roadways, bicycles are considered:
options: Vehicles that must ride with traffic and obey the same rules
questions.explain: Bicycles are vehicles on the roadway and must ride with, not against, traffic.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Bicyclists'; ORC 4511.52

questions.q: How much lane space should you give a motorcyclist?
options: The motorcycle should share with your car
Only the right third of the lane
questions.explain: Allow motorcycles a full lane width; they need space to react to traffic.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Motorcyclists'

questions.q: A motorcycle ahead has its turn signal flashing. What should you assume?
options: It may not be turning—motorcycle signals may not self-cancel
questions.explain: Motorcycle turn signals may not self-cancel; do not assume the rider is turning.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Motorcyclists'

questions.q: In ideal conditions at low speed, what minimum following distance should you keep behind a motorcycle?
options: Three seconds, increasing to four or more in poor conditions
questions.explain: Keep at least three seconds in ideal low-speed conditions and four or more when conditions are less than ideal.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Motorcyclists'

questions.q: If you cannot see a truck driver's face in the truck's side mirror:
options: The truck driver cannot see you
The truck driver can see you clearly
You should honk and stay there
You are at a safe distance
questions.explain: If you can't see the driver in the side mirror, you are in the driver's 'No Zone' blind spot.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Side No Zones'

questions.q: Behind a large truck, its blind spot can extend up to how far?
questions.explain: Large vehicles have rear blind spots that extend up to 200 feet.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Rear No Zones'

questions.q: A loaded truck at 55 mph under ideal conditions needs about how far to stop?
questions.explain: A loaded truck needs a minimum of about 335 feet—over 1½ times a passenger car's stopping distance.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Front No Zones'

questions.q: After passing a large truck, when is it safe to move back in front of it?
options: As soon as your rear bumper passes its cab
When you can see the whole front of the truck in your rear-view mirror
questions.explain: Wait until you see the entire front of the truck in your inside mirror and keep your speed.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Front No Zones'

questions.q: A truck in front of you swings left before making a right turn. What should you do?
options: Move into the space it left
Honk and pass on the left
Stay back and do not squeeze between the truck and the curb
questions.explain: Large vehicles may swing wide to turn right; never squeeze between the truck and the curb.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Turning'

questions.q: According to the Ohio manual, how much longer does it take commercial trucks to stop than cars?
options: Twice as long in all cases
questions.explain: Don't cut in front of trucks; they take about 40 percent longer to stop.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Commercial Vehicles'

questions.q: Why are you told to stop behind the stop line at intersections?
options: Only so cameras can read your plate
It gives large vehicles more room to turn
To make it easier to run the light
questions.explain: Stop lines set you back far enough for larger vehicles to have turning space.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Turning'

questions.q: When should you avoid using your horn near a bicyclist?
options: When you are close to the bicyclist
questions.explain: Avoid sounding your horn close to a bicyclist; it can startle the rider.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Bicyclists'

questions.q: Farm machinery traveling on the road at night must display:
options: No lights if it stays on the shoulder
A slow-moving-vehicle emblem and a red flashing light
questions.explain: Farm machinery must display the SMV emblem and use a red flashing light at night.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Farm Machinery'

questions.q: Horse-drawn buggies and horseback riders on Ohio roads:
options: Must stay off all state routes
Are not allowed on public roads
Have the same rights as motor vehicles and must follow the same rules
questions.explain: Animal-drawn vehicles and horseback riders have the same rights and duties as motor vehicles.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Animal-Drawn Vehicles and Horseback Riders'

questions.q: Vehicles moving slower than the flow of traffic must:
options: Use the right lane or stay as close as possible to the right edge
questions.explain: Slower vehicles must use the available right lane or keep close to the right-hand curb or edge.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Slow Moving Vehicles'; ORC 4511.31

questions.q: Pedestrians often do not obey signals or use crosswalks. As a driver you should:
options: Be ready to yield to them anyway
Proceed because they are breaking the law
Speed up to pass before they step out
questions.explain: Pedestrians can be hard to see and unpredictable; drivers must yield to them.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Pedestrians'

questions.q: When a large tractor-trailer passes you, you can make more space by:
