options: Moving to the outside portion of your lane, away from the truck
questions.explain: Leave extra room by moving to the side of your lane away from a passing tractor-trailer.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Space to the Side'

questions.q: Near weigh stations or on steep hills behind large trucks, the Ohio manual suggests:
options: Avoiding the right lane where trucks may be re-entering traffic
questions.explain: Avoid the right lanes on steep grades and near weigh stations where trucks may merge back into faster traffic.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Rear No Zones'

questions.q: What should you do when approaching school zones with flashing lights or children present?
options: Pass slower cars to clear the zone quickly
Obey the lower school speed limit and the crossing guards
questions.explain: When lights are flashing or children are present, obey the slower limit and follow crossing guards.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Pedestrians — School Zones'

questions.q: Wet roads, sand or gravel affect bicyclists:
options: Much more than motor vehicles, so give them extra care
questions.explain: These conditions affect bicycles much more than motor vehicles; be especially careful.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Bicyclists'

questions.q: When in doubt about the speed of an approaching truck or bus, you should:
options: Not turn left in front of it
Turn quickly in front of it
questions.explain: Drivers often misjudge truck speed; don't turn left in its path when unsure.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 9: Sharing the Road — 'Turning'

questions.q: Under Ohio law, when must your headlights be on?
options: From sunset to sunrise, in rain/snow/fog, and whenever your wipers are on due to weather
Only when it is completely dark
questions.explain: Headlights are required sunset to sunrise, whenever visibility is poor, and any time wipers are used for precipitation.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 7: Special Driving Situations — 'When to Use Headlights'; ORC 4513.03

questions.q: Headlights must also be on when you cannot clearly see objects how far ahead?
questions.explain: Lights are required whenever natural light does not allow you to clearly see objects 1,000 feet ahead.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 7: Special Driving Situations — 'When to Use Headlights'

questions.q: When must you switch from high beams to low beams?
options: Never at night on rural roads
questions.explain: Ohio law requires you to dim your high beams for oncoming traffic; otherwise high beams may be used whenever your headlights are on.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 7: Special Driving Situations — 'Night Driving'; ORC 4513.15

questions.q: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explain: Use low beams in fog; high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 7: Special Driving Situations — 'Driving in Fog'

questions.q: To avoid being blinded by an oncoming vehicle's headlights at night, you should look:
options: To the left side of the road
Toward the right edge of the road
questions.explain: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid momentary blindness.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 7: Special Driving Situations — 'Night Driving'

questions.q: For drivers 18 and older, which use of a cell phone while driving is generally legal in Ohio?
options: Typing a text message while creeping along in slow traffic
Watching a video in a cup holder
A hands-free call started or ended with a single touch or swipe
Holding the phone to type a text
questions.explain: Ohio's distracted driving law bans holding or supporting a device; hands-free use activated with a single touch or swipe is allowed.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 3: Be Alert — 'Distracted Driving — Drivers Age 18 and Older'; ORC 4511.204

questions.q: What is the penalty for a first violation of Ohio's hand-held device law (age 18+) within two years?
options: Up to a $150 fine and 2 points
questions.explain: First offense: 2 points and up to $150; a distracted-driving course can avoid the fine and points.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 3: Be Alert — 'Distracted Driving'

questions.q: A third (or later) hand-held device violation within two years can bring:
options: 4 points, up to a $500 fine, and a possible 90-day suspension
questions.explain: Third or more offenses in two years: 4 points, up to $500 fine, possible 90-day suspension.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 3: Be Alert — 'Distracted Driving'

questions.q: Fines for distracted driving violations are doubled when the violation occurs:
questions.explain: Distracted driving fines double in work zones.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 3: Be Alert — 'Distracted Driving'

questions.q: Drivers under 18 in Ohio may NOT use an electronic device while driving, even:
questions.explain: Under-18 drivers may not use any electronic device, even hands-free; exceptions are navigation and emergency calls.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 3: Be Alert — 'Distracted Driving — Drivers Under Age 18'; ORC 4511.205

questions.q: What is the penalty for a driver under 18 caught using an electronic device for the first time?
options: A 60-day license suspension and a $150 fine
questions.explain: First violation: 60-day suspension and $150 fine; second: 1-year suspension and $300 fine.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 3: Be Alert — 'Distracted Driving — Drivers Under Age 18'

questions.q: Which statement about Ohio's seat belt law is correct for adult drivers?
options: Drivers and front-seat passengers must wear safety belts
Only rear passengers must be belted
Belts are optional if the car has air bags
Only the driver must be belted
questions.explain: Ohio requires drivers and front-seat occupants to wear safety belts; air bags supplement, not replace, belts.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 2: Before You Drive — 'Safety Belts'; ORC 4513.263

questions.q: For drivers under 18, what is the rule about vehicle occupants?
options: No passengers are allowed at all
Occupants are limited to the number of seat belts, and everyone must be belted
Up to two extra unbelted passengers are allowed
questions.explain: For drivers under 18, occupants may not exceed the number of installed belts and all must wear them.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 2: Before You Drive — 'Safety Belts'

questions.q: How should a lap belt be worn?
options: Snug and low across the hips
questions.explain: Adjust the lap belt snug and low across the hips; otherwise you could slide out in a crash.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 2: Before You Drive — 'Safety Belts'

questions.q: Where should the shoulder belt be worn?
options: Across the shoulder and chest with little slack
questions.explain: The shoulder belt goes across your shoulder and chest with little slack; wearing it under your arm or behind your back can cause serious internal injuries in a crash.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 2: Before You Drive — 'Safety Belts'

questions.q: In Ohio, a child who is under age 4 OR weighs less than 40 pounds must ride in:
options: A child safety seat meeting federal standards
The front seat on a parent's lap
questions.explain: Children under 4 and/or under 40 pounds must be restrained in an approved child safety seat.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 6: State Laws and Penalties — 'Child Passenger Restraints'; ORC 4511.81

questions.q: In Ohio, a child aged 4 to 7 must ride in a booster seat unless the child is at least how tall?
questions.explain: Children at least 4 but under 8 must use a booster seat unless 4'9" or taller.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 6: State Laws and Penalties — 'Child Passenger Restraints'; ORC 4511.81

questions.q: Under Ohio law, children ages 8 through 15 must be:
options: Belted only in the front seat
questions.explain: Children at least 8 but not older than 15 must be properly restrained with a safety belt.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 6: State Laws and Penalties — 'Child Passenger Restraints'

questions.q: Children of what age should ride in the back seat to avoid air bag injuries?
questions.explain: Children 12 and younger should sit in the rear seat; never put a rear-facing seat in front of an active air bag.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 6: State Laws and Penalties — 'Child Passenger Restraints'

questions.q: How far should your chest be from the steering wheel to allow for air bag deployment?
questions.explain: Sit far enough back to leave 10 inches or more between your chest and the wheel, giving the air bag room to deploy.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 2: Before You Drive — 'Adjusting the Driver's Seat'

questions.q: Your vehicle's horn must be audible from at least how far?
questions.explain: A horn in good working order must be audible from 200 feet.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 2: Before You Drive — 'Vehicle Equipment Regulations'; ORC 4513.21

questions.q: Your vehicle's brake lights must be visible from at least how far when the brakes are applied?
questions.explain: Two red stop lights must be visible from 500 feet; the taillight must also be visible from 500 feet.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 2: Before You Drive — 'Vehicle Equipment Regulations'

questions.q: Which of these is an example of aggressive driving?
options: Driving below the limit in fog
Following too closely and making unsafe lane changes
questions.explain: Aggressive driving includes speeding, tailgating, unsafe lane changes, improper signaling, and ignoring signals or signs.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 3: Be Alert — 'Aggressive Driving'

questions.q: If your license shows a corrective-lens restriction, you must:
options: Carry them in the car but wearing them is optional
Always wear your glasses or contacts when driving
questions.explain: A vision restriction means you must always wear corrective lenses when driving.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 3: Be Alert — 'Vision'

questions.q: Should you wear sunglasses when driving at night?
options: No—tinted or colored lenses reduce your vision
questions.explain: Do not wear sunglasses or colored lenses at night; they reduce what you can see.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 7: Special Driving Situations — 'Night Driving'

questions.q: When is it appropriate to tap your horn?
options: When a pedestrian or bicyclist seems about to move into your path
To express anger at another driver
questions.explain: Use the horn lightly to communicate when someone may not see you; using it inappropriately can scare or anger others.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Use Your Horn'

questions.q: You see a young child alone in a hot, locked car and the child is unresponsive. What should you do?
options: Wait for the parent to return
Call 911 and, if necessary, act to remove the child, even by breaking a window
Leave a note on the windshield
questions.explain: Call 911 right away; if the child is in distress, take action to remove them. Ohio has Good Samaritan protections.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Preventing Injury from Hot Vehicles'

questions.q: If you are pulled over by police, what should you do?
options: Get out and walk to the police car
Pull over safely to the right, turn off the engine, stay in the car with hands visible
Keep driving to a gas station several miles away
Search your glovebox before the officer arrives
questions.explain: Stop safely, shift to park, turn the engine off, lower the window, stay in the car and keep your hands on the wheel.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 7: Special Driving Situations — 'Police and Traffic Stops'

questions.q: At every intersection, which scanning pattern does the manual recommend?
options: Look left, right, then left again
questions.explain: Search for cross traffic by looking left, right, then left again.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Intersections and Turning'

questions.q: A vehicle approaching from the side has its turn signal on. What should you do?
options: Wait until you are sure it is actually turning before pulling out
questions.explain: Don't assume the driver will turn—they may turn later or have forgotten to cancel the signal.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 5: Learning to Drive — 'Tips'

questions.q: You must activate your turn signal before which of these?
options: Going straight through a green light
Stopping at a red light in your lane
questions.explain: Use a turn signal when changing lanes, merging, or turning left or right.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 8: Safe Driving Tips — 'Signal Before Changing Direction'

questions.q: If you drive while your license is suspended in Ohio, you may face:
options: A first-degree misdemeanor with a fine up to $1,000 and possibly another 1-year suspension
questions.explain: Driving under suspension is a first-degree misdemeanor with a fine up to $1,000 and possible additional one-year suspension.
questions.ref: Ohio Driver Manual / Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws (ODPS online edition, accessed Oct 2026), Section 6: State Laws and Penalties — 'Driving Under Suspension'

questions.q: Can a person under 16 ride in the open bed of a pickup truck traveling over 25 mph?
options: No, unless a specific exception applies (e.g., a secured seat with a safety belt)
Yes, if the tailgate is closed
Yes, if an adult is with them
